entry.title: Real-rooted Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of crown posets and wheel and whirl matroids
entry.summary: We prove that the Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of crown order polytopes are real-rooted, settling a conjecture of Lundström and Saud Maia Leite. For each integer $r\ge3$, the crown order polytope on $2r$ elements and the rank-$r$ whirl base polytope have the same $h^*$-polynomial. The $h^*$-polynomials of the rank-$r$ wheel and whirl base polytopes, as well as every convex combination of the two, have $2r-2$ distinct negative roots. Their coefficient sequences are positive, unimodal, and strictly ultra log-concave of order $2r-2$.

entry.title: Which posets are spectra of Noetherian rings? The case of height at most one
entry.summary: A finite poset is the prime spectrum of a Noetherian ring exactly when it has no chain of three elements, that is, it is the poset of a finite bipartite graph. This answers Conjecture 5.3 of Alkass. The substance is a construction: minimal elements become curves y=g_i(x), maximal elements points, edges the incidences, arranged by interpolation. The coordinate ring of the union of the curves, localized at the chosen points, is essentially of finite type over Q and of dimension at most one. Dropping finiteness costs two conditions, both isolated by Colbert: a poset with no chain of three elements is a Noetherian spectrum exactly when it has finitely many minimal elements and any two distinct ones have finitely many common upper bounds. A variant keeping the shape of the ideals of Alkass but changing their exponents shows why that construction produces only nested neighborhoods. Constraining the ring destroys most of this freedom: normal rings leave finite disjoint unions of stars, domains a single star, local rings a point or a finite co-star. In height two the question is open in general, but the conditions conjectured by Wiegand and Wiegand are not sufficient

entry.title: Affine Higher Bruhat Orders
entry.summary: The higher Bruhat orders are partial orders originally constructed by Manin and Schechtman, with an equivalent construction from Ziegler. These partial orders generalize the weak order on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$, and the second higher Bruhat order is a poset on commutation classes of reduced words for the longest element in ${\mathfrak{S}}_n$, where covering relations correspond to braid relations. Like the weak order, each of the higher Bruhat orders is a ranked poset with unique minimal and maximal elements. Constructing analogs of the higher Bruhat orders in other settings is an area of recent interest, including recent work of Hothem for permutations in $S_{n}$. We give a construction that generalizes any interval $[\mathrm{id},w]$ in the weak order where $w$ is an element of the affine symmetric group $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_n$. Our construction recovers the classical higher Bruhat orders when $w$ is the longest element in $\mathfrak{S}_n$. Paralleling the classical case, we show that the second higher Bruhat order is a ranked poset on commutation classes of reduced words for $w\in \widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_n$, allowing us to prove a conjecture due to Elias. When $w\in \mathfrak{S}_n$, we also establish results for our higher Bruhat orders that are direct analogs of numerous results in the classical higher Bruhat orders.

entry.title: Permutations, Pattern Covers, Posets and Positivity: Part I: Patterns and Posets
entry.summary: We study permutations covered by overlapping occurrences of a consecutive pattern. Special cases of this have been studied for consecutive patterns and via the cluster method. We study enumeration sequences obtained by repeating a fixed overlap. We elicit many structural properties of such pattern covers, mainly in terms of posets whose linear extensions are in bijection with the permutations in question. The enumeration of these permutations for different patterns gives rise to a great variety of sequences, many classical, but most of them not found in the OEIS. We conjecture that, essentially, all these sequences are moments of probability measures on the real line. We develop an enumerative and order-theoretic framework for this. For overlap 1 we give a generating function whose coefficients enumerate permutations covered by any fixed pattern with any fixed number of occurrences. For overlap at most half the pattern length we derive a polynomial-time enumeration formula. We associate to each pattern, overlap, and number of occurrences a poset whose linear extensions are the corresponding permutations. The regularity of this poset construction makes possible a structural analysis that in many cases leads to enumerative formulas for large classes of patterns. We prove uniform restrictions on the local structure of the Hasse diagrams, describe their branches (pendant chains) in terms of the corresponding patterns, and characterize when the poset is a tree or chain or subdivisions of a grid. Some of these constructions yield explicit families of formulas and explain unexpected equinumerations. In a forthcoming paper we investigate the sequences arising here from a probabilistic perspective, viewing them both as point processes and as moment sequences. We also obtain integral and matrix representations for important overlap 1 and 2 classes of pattern-covering sequences.

entry.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle braid groups
entry.summary: This paper is the first in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. These groups have two intrinsically related stories. They were first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265 by looking at spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2πi}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2π(k-1)}{k}}\}$. The $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. The second story starts from the poset of $k$-shuffle partitions, which were introduced by Drew Armstrong and explored in depth in his thesis arXiv:math/0611106. In this paper, we focus on the combinatorial aspects of $k$-shuffle braid groups starting from the poset of $k$-shuffle non-crossing partitions. We build a CW-complex on which the groups act freely, properly discontinuously and cocompactly, which we show is CAT(0) for dimension up to 7. For higher dimension, we show that the CAT(0) property is implied by the conjecture of Brady and McCammond that the dual braid complex is CAT(0) (arXiv:0909.4778).
entry.arxiv:comment: This is the first paper in a series of two, with the second one to be uploaded later in the week

entry.title: An inclusion coupling of prefix laws and the Chan-Pak rank inequality for all finite posets
entry.summary: Let $P$ be a finite poset, let $x\in P$, and let $N_k$ count its linear extensions in which $x$ occupies position $k$. We prove Chan and Pak's conjecture that, for all integers $a,h\ge1$, \[ (a+h-1)N_{a+h-1}N_a\ \ge\ (a-1)N_{a-1}N_{a+h}+hN_aN_{a+h}. \] The key result is an inclusion coupling of the laws of the set of elements preceding $x$, conditional on consecutive positions of $x$. We construct reversible exchange chains on the corresponding layers of order ideals and couple their generators so that the two prefix sets remain nested. Fishburn's correlation inequality gives monotonicity of endpoint probabilities; their unit total masses provide the rate bounds needed for the coupling. A stationary distribution of the coupled chain then has the required marginals. Normalized cover observables yield a four-term nonnegative certificate for the case $h=1$, and the general case follows by telescoping. The argument applies at every width and gives a proof of Stanley's log-concavity inequality with Fishburn's inequality as its sole external inequality.

entry.title: Strong $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Actions and Symmetric Chain Decompositions
entry.summary: We introduce a notion of a strong $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action on a poset, and conjecture the existence of such an action is equivalent to the existence of a symmetric chain decomposition of that poset. We explain the intuition behind the conjecture, go through a number of explicit examples, and prove some special cases and relaxations of the conjecture. Then we explain a computational experiment where we tested the conjecture on millions of randomly constructed rank-symmetric, rank-unimodal, and strongly Sperner posets.

entry.title: Alternating Hamilton Paths and Cycles in Poset Products
entry.summary: We study alternating Hamilton paths and cycles in the comparability graphs of finite posets. We prove that if a finite poset $P$ with at least two elements admits an alternating Hamilton path, then $P\times B_r$ admits an alternating Hamilton cycle for every $r\ge2$, where $B_r$ is the Boolean lattice. As a corollary, we settle a conjecture of Katona [Discrete Appl. Math., 2013]. Furthermore, we characterize the divisor lattices admitting alternating Hamilton paths and cycles.

entry.title: Regularity of Totally Nonnegative Wonderful Compactification
entry.summary: Let $G$ be a split real semisimple group of adjoint type. We prove that the cellular decomposition of the totally nonnegative part of its wonderful compactification is a regular CW complex, confirming a conjecture of Galashin, Karp, and Lam. In particular, the closure of every cell is homeomorphic to a closed ball. The proof combines a Bruhat atlas compatible with total positivity and a CL-labeling of the augmented face poset. The atlas models the strata locally with open Richardson varieties in the flag variety of a larger Kac-Moody group and identifies their totally nonnegative cells.

entry.title: The Bounded-Linear Dichotomy Holds for all 4 Point Posets
entry.summary: Given a finite poset $\mathcal P$, its induced saturation number, $\text{sat}^*(n,\mathcal P)$ is the smallest size a family of subsets of $[n]$ can have such that it does not contain an induced copy of $\mathcal P$, but adding any other set to it creates one. The saturation numbers already show a sharp dichotomy -- Freschi, Piga, Sharifzadeh and Treglown showed that for any given poset its saturation number is either bounded or at least $2\sqrt n$. The dominant conjecture is that in fact, the saturation numbers are either bounded, or exactly linear. In this paper we show that this dichotomy is true for all posets on at most 4 points. Most of these posets, most notably the butterfly and the diamond, had individually long resisted analysis, and the missing piece which this paper tackles is the poset comprised of a $\mathcal V$ and an isolated point, denoted by $\widehat{\mathcal V}$, for which we show linear saturation. The architecture of the proof uncovers the structure of an arbitrary $\widehat{\mathcal V}$- saturated family, namely an antichain with at most two chains above it, and an upside-down forest below it. Moreover, we anticipate that, at least partially, this structure is relevant to the wider class of posets that contain an isolated point.

entry.title: Restrictions of the dot action representation
entry.summary: Regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties are subvarieties of flag varieties defined for any reductive group. Their cohomology carries a representation of the associated Weyl group, known as the dot action representation. In type $A$, these representations can be computed using the chromatic quasisymmetric functions of naturally labeled unit interval graphs. We prove that restricting the dot action representation of any Weyl group to a type $A$ parabolic subgroup yields a representation isomorphic to a direct sum of type $A$ dot action representations. This work is motivated by the conjecture that an analogous property holds for all parabolic subgroups. In particular, for classical Weyl groups of types $B/C$ and $D$, we use chromatic symmetric functions to provide a streamlined, combinatorial formula for the restriction to a specific maximal type $A$ parabolic subgroup. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Lesnevich regarding the representations associated with ideals of types $B$ and $C$ identified under the standard poset isomorphism. Specifically, we show that the corresponding dot action representations are isomorphic if and only if the ideals determine the same reflection sets in their respective root systems. Furthermore, we show that a Catalan number counts the total number of such ideals.

entry.title: Magnitude of module categories and special biserial algebras
entry.summary: Børve, Horiatakis, and Kalck defined the magnitude of the module category of a representation-finite algebra as the sum of the entries of the inverse of the matrix of Hom dimensions between indecomposable modules. They showed it is an Euler characteristic, the alternating count of vertices, arrows, and meshes of the Auslander--Reiten quiver, and conjectured that it is at least the number of simple modules, with equality precisely for special biserial algebras. We prove this conjecture over an algebraically closed field. For a representation-directed algebra, we relate the magnitudes of the module category, the subcategory of modules without a given simple composition factor, and the ideal quotient by it. By the theory of hammocks of Ringel and Vossieck, this quotient is equivalent to a category of representations of a finite poset, whose magnitude we compute. The general case reduces to the representation-directed case through algebras obtained by grading a standard form.
entry.arxiv:comment: 33 pages, comments welcome! Lean formalization of the main result is available at https://haruhisa-enomoto.github.io/magnitude-conjecture/

entry.title: The Kelly--Trotter conjecture and dimension of poset products
entry.summary: We study the order dimension of Cartesian products of finite posets. Kelly and Trotter conjectured in 1982 that $\dim(P\times Q)\ge\dim P+\dim Q-2$ for all finite posets $P$ and $Q$. For $m\ge3$, let $R_m$ denote the incidence poset of the complete graph on $m$ vertices. We prove that there is a constant $C$ such that, for all sufficiently large $m$, $\dim(R_m\times R_m)\le\left(1+\frac{2}{\log_2 6}\right)\dim R_m+C$. Since $1+2/\log_2 6<2$, this disproves the Kelly--Trotter conjecture and shows that $2\dim R_m-2-\dim(R_m\times R_m)$ can grow linearly with $\dim R_m$. For every integer $d\ge8$, we construct an incidence poset $Q_d$ such that $\dim Q_d=d$ and $Q_d$ has the $(3,d)$-covering property. Consequently, $\dim(P\times Q_d)\le\dim P+d-3$ for every poset $P$ with $\dim P\ge3$. Thus, for every integer $d\ge8$, the poset $Q_d$ violates the Kelly--Trotter conjecture with every poset of dimension at least $3$. Finally, we prove that a poset $Q$ has an $(r,s)$-covering if and only if $\dim(Q\times C^r)\le s$ for every finite chain $C$ with at least two elements.

entry.title: Proof of the Kahn Saks Conjecture
entry.summary: Let $\mathbb{P}(x\prec y)$ be the probability that $x$ precedes $y$ in a uniformly random linear extension of an $n$-element poset $P$, and define the balancing coefficient to be $δ(x,y)=\min(\mathbb{P}(x\prec y),\mathbb{P}(y\prec x))$ with $δ(P)=\max_{x,y}δ(x,y)$. We prove (Theorem 1) that sufficiently large width forces $δ(P)$ to be arbitrarily close to $1/2$, answering a long-standing conjecture of Kahn and Saks. In fact, we prove the stronger result (Theorem 2) that large width forces one of two configurations in our poset: either a nearly uniform order on $k$ vertices, or an almost fixed order on $t$ vertices with one further vertex inserted uniformly among the $t+1$ slots. We also show that, for fixed $k$, the first possibility must occur within any antichain $X$ of size $Ω(n^{2/3})$.

entry.title: Breaking the Infinite Barrier in the $\frac{1}{3}$--$\frac{2}{3}$ Conjecture
entry.summary: The balance constant is a poset parameter measuring how well random linear extensions can be split according to their relative order on two elements. We give an $\varepsilon$-improvement for the balance constant over the bound by Brightwell, Felsner and Trotter (1995), for some small $\varepsilon>0$. This is the first general result towards the $\frac{1}{3}$--$\frac{2}{3}$ conjecture in over 30 years.
entry.arxiv:comment: 32 pages, v2 simplifies the proof of Lemmas 4.2 and 6.4

entry.title: Antichain polynomials of products of chains and minuscule posets
entry.summary: This paper studies the antichain polynomials of $[k]\times P$, where $P$ is a connected minuscule poset. We give a formula for the number of antichains, counted by size, of an arbitrary poset. Using this formula, we present necessary and sufficient conditions for the palindromicity of antichain polynomials for two infinite families of connected minuscule posets. We show that, for every connected minuscule poset $P$, if the antichain polynomial of $[k]\times P$ is palindromic, then it has only real and strictly negative zeros. This result, in particular, gives an affirmative answer to Ding-Dong's conjecture about $γ$-positivity of the antichain polynomial of $[k]\times P$. By constructing a bijection between antichains and labeled Dyck paths, we also give a layer-refined enumeration of the antichains in $[2]\times[m]\times[n]$. We establish a relation between such antichains and Clar covers of the hexagonal flakes $O(2,m,n)$, thus prove a conjectured determinantal formula for a family of Zhang-Zhang polynomials. Real-rootedness and stability results are also obtained when the shortest chain has length at most two. Finally, we present infinitely many connected Peck posets whose antichain polynomials are not unimodal, disproving the log-concavity conjecture of Ding and Dong.

entry.title: An Introduction to the Lagrange and Markov Spectra through the Lens of Generalized Markov Numbers
entry.summary: This text is a self-contained expository survey of the Lagrange and Markov spectra, centered on a comprehensive exposition of Markov's theorem and its generalizations. Its purpose is to provide a systematic text for learning the theory, with detailed proofs and explanations of the connections among its arithmetic, combinatorial, and geometric descriptions. The necessary background in continued fractions, quadratic irrationals, binary quadratic forms, and bi-infinite sequences is developed step by step, followed by an exposition of generalized Markov numbers, fence posets, curve lengths, and generalized Cohn matrices. One goal of this exposition is to explain the formula connecting generalized Markov numbers with the two spectra. For nonnegative integer parameters $(k_1,k_2,k_3)$, a permutation $σ\in\mathfrak S_3$, and a fraction label $t\in\mathbb Q_{\geq0}\cup\{\infty\}$, let $m_t$ be the associated generalized Markov number and let $k_t=k_{i_t}$ be the parameter assigned to its position $i_t\in\{1,2,3\}$. The text explains the construction of an associated finite sequence $S(t)$ of positive integers and the identity \[ \mathcal L(α_{S(t)}) =\mathcal M(Q_{S(t)}) =\frac{\sqrt{((3+k_1+k_2+k_3)m_t-k_t)^2-4}}{m_t}, \] where $α_{S(t)}=[\overline{S(t)}]$ and $Q_{S(t)}=(x-α_{S(t)}y)(x-α'_{S(t)}y)$, with the prime denoting quadratic conjugation. Here $\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal M$ denote the Lagrange and Markov constants, respectively. The survey explains how this identity relates generalized discrete Markov spectra to the classical theory and how Markov's theorem is recovered when the parameters vanish. The account also includes boundary values arising from irrational slopes and generalizations of Frobenius's uniqueness conjecture, providing a unified perspective on the classical theorem and its extensions.
entry.arxiv:comment: 184 pages. A self-contained expository survey of the Lagrange and Markov spectra and their connections with generalized Markov numbers, with detailed proofs and examples

entry.title: On the Tutte polynomial of series-parallel posets
entry.summary: The Tutte polynomial is a bivariate polynomial that has been extensively studied in graph and matroid theory. Gordon was the first to study the Tutte polynomial $T(P;x,y)$ of the greedoid induced by a poset $P$, including the special case of series-parallel posets. In particular, Gordon and McMahon conjectured that, for any two series-parallel posets $P$ and $Q$, the equality $T(P;x,y)=T(Q;x,y)$ holds if and only if $P\cong Q$. In studying this conjecture, Gordon introduced a subclass $\mathcal{P}$ of series-parallel posets and proved that this equivalence holds for all $P,Q\in\mathcal{P}$. In this paper, we introduce a new subclass $\mathrm H$ of series-parallel posets and prove that $\mathcal P\subseteq\mathrm H$. Moreover, we show that, for every $P\in\mathrm H$ and every $Q\in\mathrm{SP}$, the equality $T(P;x,y)=T(Q;x,y)$ holds if and only if $P\cong Q$, thereby extending Gordon's result.

entry.title: The Hibi-Li Face-Number Conjecture
entry.summary: We prove the face-number conjecture of Hibi and Li: for every finite poset, the order polytope has no more faces of any given dimension than the chain polytope. More generally, the face numbers increase weakly along the admissible family of chain--order polytopes when one order coordinate is replaced by a chain coordinate. We also prove that, unless the order and chain polytopes are unimodularly equivalent, all face-number inequalities in dimensions $2,\ldots,|P|-1$ are strict.
entry.arxiv:comment: 17 pages, added proof of strict inequality conjecture

entry.title: Embedding rooted blow-ups of tree posets
entry.summary: A tree poset $T$ is a poset whose Hasse diagram is a tree. Bukh proved that if a family $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ contains $(h(T)-1+\varepsilon)\binom{n}{\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\rfloor}$ sets, then $\mathcal F$ contains a weak copy of $T$, where $h(T)$ is the height of $T$, the number of elements in a longest chain of $T$. Several strengthenings and generalizations of this result have been obtained. We prove the following robust variant. For a tree poset $T$ and $x\in T$, the $b$-blow-up $T(x,b)$ rooted at $x$ is the tree poset that we obtain from $T$ by replacing every element $u$ by $b^d$ new elements, where $d$ is the distance $d(x,u)$ in the Hasse diagram of $T$ and an edge $uv$ with $v$ being closer to $x$ is replaced by edges such that every new copy of $v$ is joined to $b$ new copies of $u$ such that these new copies form pairwise disjoint sets for the copies of $v$. We prove that for any tree poset $T$, $x\in T$, and $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $δ$ such that if $\mathcal F\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ contains $(h(T)-1+\varepsilon)\binom{n}{\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\rfloor}$ sets, then $\mathcal F$ contains a weak copy of $T(x,\lfloor δn\rfloor)$. This settles a conjecture of Treglown and the author. As applications, we derive the known asymptotic counting and random versions of Bukh's theorem from this stronger embedding result, and obtain new maximal anti-Ramsey results for tree posets.
